newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-HOLDERS JUVENTUS SWEEP ASIDE ROSENBORG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HOLDERS JUVENTUS SWEEP ASIDE ROSENBORG.

text.p: Defending champions Juventus swept aside Norwegian outsiders Rosenborg 2-0 on Wednesday to reach the semifinals of the European Cup where they will face Ajax in a replay of last year's final.
The straightforward quarter-final second leg win, which earned a 3-1 aggregate victory, came courtesy of a gift goal in the first half and a penalty in the dying seconds.
"We are in the semifinal again," said Juventus coach Marcello Lippi, who led the Italian side to penalty shoot-out glory against Ajax last year in Rome's Olympic Stadium.
"The boys have got a bit used to these good results and we hope to go all the way," he said.
"But it is harder to defend a title than to win it."
Rosenborg ended the match with 10 men after Stale Stensaas was sent off in the 88th minute for protesting against the penalty decision but the game was over as a contest long before that.
Zinedine Zidane got Juventus under way after 29 minutes and the French international midfielder can rarely have had an easier chance.
Rosenborg goalkeeper Joern Jamtfall mis-hit a clearance that skewed straight at Zidane, just outside the area, who hit it straight back into the empty net.
"I've never seen anything like it at this level," said Lippi.
Jamtfall made up for his error later, with some brave saves when Juventus players were clear on goal.

Zidane, asked if he had actually hit the ball or just let it effortlessly rebound off his right leg, was adamant that he deserved fuller credit than many were giving him. "I saw it coming and I put my foot out," he said.

Croat striker Alen Boksic, who had played only 10 minutes of soccer since getting injured in January, came on as a late first half substitute for Christian Vieri, who suffered a bruised and twisted ankle in one of the many tussles.
Boksic should have scored at least twice, breaking through but never getting past Jamtfall.
"It was a good thing Zidane scored, it doesn't matter how he did it," Boksic said, recognising that his team squandered plenty of chances. "There's room for those kind of goals."
Nicola Amoruso scored the second, a last minute penalty, after Attilio Lombardo was felled.
The scoreline flattered the Norwegians, who dumped AC Milan out of the cup at the Champions League' stage.
It took them 75 minutes to force their first and only corner against a Juve side that was always in control.
"I thought they were better in Trondheim," said Lippi, who declared himself fully satisfied with the team, saying it was always going to be difficult to break down opponents who packed the midfield.
Rosenborg coach Nils Eggen congratulated his opponents and recognised they had been far better on the night.
"We had a very bad first half. When we were attacking more in the second half and moved some 20 metres up the field, we gave them one or two problems," he said.
"I think the players were a little bit surprised by the aggression of the Juventus team."
Teams:

Juventus: 1-Angelo Peruzzi; 2-Ciro Ferrara, 4-Paolo Montero, 5-Sergio Porrini, 7-Angelo Di Livio (19-Attilio Lombardo 76), 13-Mark Iuliano, 14-Didier Deschamps, 15-Christian Vieri (9-Alen Boksic 44), 16-Nicola Amoruso, 18-Vladimir Jugovic, 21-Zinedine Zidane (20-Alessio Tacchinardi 82).

Rosenborg: 1-Joern Jamtfall; 3-Erik Hoftun, 5-Stale Stensaas (red card 88), 6-Roar Strand (10-Harald Brattbakk 59), 8-Bent Skammelsrud, 11-Mini Jakobsen (17-Karl Oskar Fjoertoft 67), 14-Vegard Heggem, 15-Jon Olav Hjelde, 20-Trond Egil Soltvedt, 26-Sigurd Rushfeldt, 27-Andre Bergdoelmo.
